CUDA-Q QEC C++ API

Code

class code : public cudaqx::extension_point<code, const heterogeneous_map&>

Base class for quantum error correcting codes in CUDA-Q.

This class provides the core interface and functionality for implementing quantum error correcting codes in CUDA-Q. It defines the basic operations that any QEC code must support and provides infrastructure for syndrome measurement and error correction experiments.

To implement a new quantum error correcting code:

  1. Create a new class that inherits from code

  2. Implement the protected virtual methods:

    • get_num_data_qubits()

    • get_num_ancilla_qubits()

    • get_num_ancilla_x_qubits()

    • get_num_ancilla_z_qubits()

  3. Define quantum kernels for each required logical operation (these are the fault tolerant logical operation implementations)

  4. Register the operations in your constructor using the operation_encodings map on the base class

  5. Register your new code type using CUDAQ_EXT_PT_REGISTER_TYPE

Example implementation: 

__qpu__ void x_kernel(patch p);
__qpu__ void z_kernel(patch p);
class my_code : public qec::code {
protected:
  std::size_t get_num_data_qubits() const override { return 7; }
  std::size_t get_num_ancilla_qubits() const override { return 6; }
  std::size_t get_num_ancilla_x_qubits() const override { return 3; }
  std::size_t get_num_ancilla_z_qubits() const override { return 3; }

public:
  my_code(const heterogeneous_map& options) : code() {
    // Can use user-specified options, e.g. auto d =
    options.get<int>("distance");
    operation_encodings.insert(std::make_pair(operation::x, x_kernel));
    operation_encodings.insert(std::make_pair(operation::z, z_kernel));
    // Register other required operations...

    // Define the default stabilizers!
    m_stabilizers = qec::stabilizers({"XXXX", "ZZZZ"});
  }

  CUDAQ_EXTENSION_CUSTOM_CREATOR_FUNCTION(
    my_code,
    static std::unique_ptr<qec::code> create(const heterogeneous_map
&options) { return std::make_unique<my_code>(options);
    }
  )
};

CUDAQ_EXT_PT_REGISTER_TYPE(my_code)

Supported quantum operations for error correcting codes

Subclassed by cudaq::qec::repetition::repetition, cudaq::qec::steane::steane, cudaq::qec::surface_code::surface_code

Public Types

using one_qubit_encoding = cudaq::qkernel<void(patch)>

Type alias for single qubit quantum kernels.

using two_qubit_encoding = cudaq::qkernel<void(patch, patch)>

Type alias for two qubit quantum kernels.

using stabilizer_round = cudaq::qkernel<std::vector<cudaq::measure_result>(patch, const std::vector<std::size_t>&, const std::vector<std::size_t>&)>

Type alias for stabilizer measurement kernels. The two vector arguments are the flattened X and Z stabilizer schedule matrices (see get_stabilizer_schedule_x/z()): entry 0 = no support, entry k >= 1 = interaction at timestep k.

using encoding = std::variant<one_qubit_encoding, two_qubit_encoding, stabilizer_round>

Type alias for quantum operation encodings.

inline virtual cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t> get_stabilizer_schedule_x() const

Get the X-stabilizer schedule matrix passed to the code’s stabilizer_round kernel. Same shape and support pattern as get_parity_x(); entry 0 means no support, entry k >= 1 means the ancilla-data interaction executes at timestep k, so a code can encode an optimized (e.g. hook-error-aware) gate order.

Returns:

Tensor of scheduled interactions; the default implementation returns get_parity_x() unchanged (every interaction at timestep 1, i.e. ascending qubit-index order).

inline virtual cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t> get_stabilizer_schedule_z() const

Get the Z-stabilizer schedule matrix passed to the code’s stabilizer_round kernel. See get_stabilizer_schedule_x().

Returns:

Tensor of scheduled interactions; the default implementation returns get_parity_z() unchanged.

struct patch

Represents a logical qubit patch for quantum error correction.

This type is for CUDA-Q kernel code only.

This structure defines a patch of qubits used in quantum error correction codes. It consists of data qubits and ancilla qubits for X and Z stabilizer measurements.

enum class cudaq::qec::surface_code::sc_orientation

Surface-code orientation: controls which Pauli type (X or Z) occupies the bulk interior and which boundaries are X-type vs Z-type.

Geometry names follow the NVIDIA/Ising-Decoding naming convention (https://github.com/NVIDIA/Ising-Decoding): Ising’s code_rotation convention uses first character = bulk syndrome type, second character = rotated_type. By geometry: XV and ZH place X-type stabilizers on the left/right boundaries (Z on top/bottom); XH and ZV place X-type on top/bottom (Z on left/right). XV vs ZH (and XH vs ZV) differ in the bulk X/Z checkerboard.

Observable convention: get_spin_op_observables() returns the valid logical pair for the orientation. XV/ZH use X obs along the top row and Z obs along the left column; XH/ZV swap them (X along the left column, Z along the top row). See get_spin_op_observables() for details.

Values:

enumerator XV
enumerator XH
enumerator ZV
enumerator ZH
struct vec2d

describes the 2d coordinate on the stabilizer grid

class stabilizer_grid

Generates and keeps track of the 2d grid of stabilizers in the rotated surface code. Following same layout convention as in: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10687 Grid layout is arranged from left to right, top to bottom (row major storage) grid_length = 4 example: 

(0,0)   (0,1)   (0,2)   (0,3)
(1,0)   (1,1)   (1,2)   (1,3)
(2,0)   (2,1)   (2,2)   (2,3)
(3,0)   (3,1)   (3,2)   (3,3)
Each entry on the grid can be an X stabilizer, Z stabilizer, or empty, as is needed on the edges. The diagrams below show the default ZH orientation. Other orientations assign X/Z roles according to sc_orientation. The grid length of 4 corresponds to a distance 3 surface code, which results in: 
e(0,0)  e(0,1)  Z(0,2)  e(0,3)
X(1,0)  Z(1,1)  X(1,2)  e(1,3)
e(2,0)  X(2,1)  Z(2,2)  X(2,3)
e(3,0)  Z(3,1)  e(3,2)  e(3,3)

This is seen through the print_stabilizer_grid() member function. To get rid of the empty sites, the print_stabilizer_coords() function is used: 

                Z(0,2)
X(1,0)  Z(1,1)  X(1,2)
        X(2,1)  Z(2,2)  X(2,3)
        Z(3,1)

and to get the familiar visualization of the distance three surface code, the print_stabilizer_indices results in: 

        Z0
X0  Z1  X1
    X2  Z2  X3
    Z3

The data qubits are located at the four corners of each of the weight-4 stabilizers. They are also organized with index increasing from left to right, top to bottom: 

d0  d1  d2
d3  d4  d5
d6  d7  d8

std::vector<cudaq::spin_op_term> get_spin_op_stabilizers() const

Get the stabilizers as a vector of cudaq::spin_op_terms.

cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t> get_cnot_schedule_x() const

Get the CNOT schedule matrix for the X stabilizers.

Note

The per-plaquette CNOT order is chosen per the grid’s orientation so that mid-round ancilla faults (“hook errors”), which propagate onto the data qubits of the remaining CNOTs, land perpendicular to the same-type logical operator instead of along it, following the standard zigzag schedule of https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.3747. Rows are ordered to match the rows of to_parity_matrix() / code::get_parity_x().

Returns:

Tensor with the same shape and support pattern as the X block of the parity check matrix (num_x_stabilizers x distance^2). Entry 0 means the ancilla does not touch that data qubit; entry k in [1, 4] means the ancilla-data CNOT executes at timestep k of the stabilizer round.

cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t> get_cnot_schedule_z() const

Get the CNOT schedule matrix for the Z stabilizers.

Note

See get_cnot_schedule_x() for the hook-error rationale and row ordering.

Returns:

Tensor with the same shape and support pattern as the Z block of the parity check matrix (num_z_stabilizers x distance^2). Entry 0 means the ancilla does not touch that data qubit; entry k in [1, 4] means the data-ancilla CNOT executes at timestep k of the stabilizer round.

std::vector<std::size_t> get_cnot_schedule_pairs_x() const

Get the X-stabilizer CNOT schedule as a flat list of (stabilizer index, data index) pairs, ordered by timestep within each stabilizer — the replay format for kernels that take an explicit CNOT pair list. Stabilizer indices match the rows of get_cnot_schedule_x().

std::vector<std::size_t> get_cnot_schedule_pairs_z() const

Z-stabilizer counterpart of get_cnot_schedule_pairs_x().

std::vector<cudaq::spin_op_term> get_spin_op_observables() const

Get the observables as a vector of cudaq::spin_op_terms.

Note

Returns the correct logical pair for the grid’s orientation. For XV and ZH the X observable runs along the top row of data qubits and the Z observable along the left column; for XH and ZV the assignment is swapped (X along the left column, Z along the top row) to match their boundary types. The returned X/Z observables commute with the stabilizers and anticommute with each other for every orientation.

Returns:

The X logical observable first, followed by the Z logical observable.

Detector Error Model

struct detector_error_model

A detector error model (DEM) for a quantum error correction circuit. A DEM can be created from a QEC circuit and a noise model. It contains information about which errors flip which detectors. This is used by the decoder to help make predictions about observables flips.

Shared size parameters among the matrix types.

  • detector_error_matrix: num_detectors x num_error_mechanisms [d, e]

  • error_rates: num_error_mechanisms

  • observables_flips_matrix: num_observables x num_error_mechanisms [k, e]

Note

The C++ API for this class may change in the future. The Python API is more likely to be backwards compatible.

Public Functions

std::size_t num_detectors() const

Return the number of rows in the detector_error_matrix.

std::size_t num_error_mechanisms() const

Return the number of columns in the detector_error_matrix, error_rates, and observables_flips_matrix.

std::size_t num_observables() const

Return the number of rows in the observables_flips_matrix.

void canonicalize_for_rounds(uint32_t num_syndromes_per_round, bool remove_zero_syndrome_errors = false)

Put the detector_error_matrix into canonical form for round-based decoding: topologically order the columns and merge columns that share the same detector AND observable signature, composing their rates so the canonicalized model matches the input.

Note

Canonicalization does not preserve cross-column exclusivity structure: each output column is given a fresh unique error id and is treated as independent, so any error_ids correlation in the input model is discarded.

Parameters:

  • num_syndromes_per_round – Number of syndromes per round, used to order columns by the rounds their detectors span; 0 disables the per-round key.

  • remove_zero_syndrome_errors – If false (default), zero-syndrome columns that still flip an observable (undetectable logical errors) are retained so the observable-flip probability is preserved; if true, all columns with no detector signature are dropped (appropriate when the DEM is consumed only for round-based decoding).

void canonicalize_for_rounds_with_boundary(uint32_t num_syndromes_per_round, uint32_t num_boundary_syndromes, bool remove_zero_syndrome_errors)

Boundary-aware variant of canonicalize_for_rounds for memory-experiment DEMs whose first and last detector layers (the boundaries) are narrower than the interior layers.

Parameters:

  • num_syndromes_per_round – Interior-layer width (syndromes per interior round).

  • num_boundary_syndromes – Width of the leading and trailing boundary layers: the first and last num_boundary_syndromes rows form the boundary rounds and each intermediate block of num_syndromes_per_round rows is an interior round.

  • remove_zero_syndrome_errors – Same meaning as in the scalar overload.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – if num_syndromes_per_round is 0 or num_boundary_syndromes > num_syndromes_per_round.

Public Members

cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t> detector_error_matrix

The detector error matrix is a specific kind of circuit-level parity-check matrix where each row represents a detector, and each column represents an error mechanism. The entries of this matrix are H[i,j] = 1 if detector i is triggered by error mechanism j, and 0 otherwise.

std::vector<double> error_rates

The list of weights has length equal to the number of columns of detector_error_matrix, which assigns a likelihood to each error mechanism.

cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t> observables_flips_matrix

The observables flips matrix is a specific kind of circuit-level parity- check matrix where each row represents a Pauli observable, and each column represents an error mechanism. The entries of this matrix are O[i,j] = 1 if Pauli observable i is flipped by error mechanism j, and 0 otherwise.

std::optional<std::vector<std::size_t>> error_ids

Error mechanism ID. From a probability perspective, each error mechanism ID is independent of all other error mechanism ID. For all errors with the same ID, only one of them can happen. That is - the errors containing the same ID are correlated with each other.

detector_error_model cudaq::qec::dem_from_stim_text(const std::string &dem_text, bool use_decomp_suggestions = false)

Parse the Stim DEM string dem_text into detector/observable flip matrices and error rates. DEM-native decoders should consume raw DEM text instead. By default (use_decomp_suggestions = false) the ‘^’ separators are ignored and each error instruction produces a single column. If use_decomp_suggestions is true, error mechanisms that carry an explicit graphlike decomposition (components separated by ‘^’) are expanded into one column per component, each inheriting the probability of the parent instruction. error_ids is always left as nullopt. Note that this is a lossy approximation of the original DEM.

Dynamic DEM

Types for constructing a dynamic detector error model (DEM). See the Dynamic Detector Error Models and the Decoding with a Dynamic DEM example.

struct dem_chunks_spec

Multi-phase DEM decomposition with arbitrary named phases.

Standard memory experiment (linear chain A → B×N → C): connections = [{init,bulk}, {bulk,bulk}, {bulk,final}] seam = {next_round, prev_round} num_rounds = T (omit for streaming — num_rounds unknown at config time)

dem_chunks_from_spec() calls phase_sequence() to materialise the full ordered chunk list. num_rounds is only needed for that call: phase_sequence() throws when a self-loop is present and num_rounds is absent. For a linear chain (no self-loop) phase_sequence() derives the length from the connections.

std::vector<phase_id> phase_sequence() const

Expand connections + num_rounds into an ordered phase_id list.

With a self-loop (repeating phase) and num_rounds = T: result = [A, B, B, …(T-2 times)…, B, C] Without a self-loop, the sequence length is derived from the connections and num_rounds is not consulted.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – if a self-loop is present and num_rounds is absent, or if the connection graph is not a valid linear chain: a phase with more than one non-self outgoing edge, or a cycle among the non-self edges, is rejected.

Also checks that every connection names a phase with a spec, the phases agree on the observable count, observable_names has one unique name per observable, and no repeating phase carries m2o_sparse, which has one row per observable inside its round: its measurement count with D_sparse, else its detectors.

std::optional<bool> phases_supply_D_sparse

Whether the phases supply D, where the emptiness of their D_sparse rows cannot say so on its own. Carries no rows itself: it only settles how has_D_sparse() reads the ones the phases carry.

Unset infers it: any phase carrying rows means the spec supplies D, which is what every spec written before this field did and what a memory experiment needs. Set it only where emptiness is ambiguous &#8212; true declares that the phases supply D even where one of them contributes no detector rows at all, false keeps the dem_chunks_to_d_sparse() memory convention even though rows are present. struct dem_chunk_spec

One DEM phase/chunk as flat index lists.

Two mutually exclusive forms:

Shorthand: H_sparse at chunk level. The expander assigns this single H to every seam named in the connection (all seams share the same H rows). Valid for CSS memory experiments where prev_round.H == next_round.H.

Full per-seam: seam_specs populated directly with per-seam H_sparse and O_sparse. Required when seams carry different H rows (non-memory gadgets).

O_sparse at chunk level maps to extended_dem::O (the decoder observable).

Expand H_sparse shorthand into seam_specs using the provided IDs.

No-op when seam_specs is already populated. The shorthand H_sparse is assigned to every seam in ids with an empty O_sparse.

Parameters:

ids – Seam IDs to create entries for (e.g. {next_round, prev_round})

std::vector<std::int64_t> H_sparse

Shorthand: shared H for all seams. Mutually exclusive with seam_specs.

std::vector<seam_spec_entry> seam_specs

Full per-seam form. Mutually exclusive with H_sparse.

std::vector<std::int64_t> O_sparse

Chunk-level observable rows → extended_dem::O.

std::vector<std::int64_t> D_sparse

Optional measurement-to-detector rows in the -1-terminated encoding, one per detector this chunk contributes when closed: its to_seam rows, then its interior rows. Indices count the previous round’s measurements first and then this round’s own: index j is the previous round’s measurement j when j is below that round’s measurement count, and otherwise this round’s measurement j minus that count. Either every phase of a dem_chunks_spec carries rows or none does; with none, D follows the memory-experiment convention of dem_chunks_to_d_sparse().

The window is those two rounds and no further back, which bounds what a measurement-free phase can sit between. Such a phase &#8212; a transversal Clifford, a state preparation &#8212; may form its own detectors from the round before it, but it then leaves that round unreachable to the phase after it, whose window starts at its own first measurement. A chain that must difference across such a gadget cannot say so here.

std::optional<uint64_t> num_measurements

Measurements this phase’s round adds to the stream, when it differs from dem_chunks_spec::measurements_per_round (a final data readout, say). Like that field, it applies when the phases carry D_sparse rows; without them a round adds one measurement per detector.

std::vector<std::int64_t> m2o_sparse

Optional readout map, -1-terminated: one row per observable, listing the measurements of this phase’s own round whose parity this round adds to the observable’s raw value (the XOR over every round that reads it); an empty row adds nothing. A repeating phase may not carry it. The round has its measurement count when the phases carry D_sparse rows, else one measurement per detector.

H_sparse and O_sparse use the -1-terminated row encoding: [0, 1, 5, -1, 1, 2, 6, -1] describes two rows.

struct seam_id

Lightweight identifier for a named seam or phase.

The value is the FNV1a-32 hash of the name string, computed at compile time. Two seam_ids are equal iff they were constructed from the same name. The same string always produces the same ID, so no registry is required for identity comparison. A name registry is available via register_name() and name() for human-readable diagnostics and error messages.

dem_chunks_spec cudaq::qec::memory_dem_chunks_from_decoder_inputs(const decoder_inputs &inputs, std::size_t extraction_rounds, std::size_t measurements_per_round, std::size_t final_measurements)

Split a characterized memory circuit into reusable DEM phases.

The input records contain extraction_rounds groups of measurements_per_round bits followed by final_measurements data readout bits. Each detector is assigned to the round containing its latest measurement. Its D row may read that round and its immediate predecessor only. Detector numbering must already be round-major. Each independent fault must touch a detector and span at most two consecutive detector rounds. Up to 64 observables are supported.

Consecutive phases matching the middle round are collapsed into one bulk phase with a self-loop. At least two matching rounds are required as evidence of repetition. Prefix and suffix transients are retained separately. Rates must agree within a relative tolerance of 1e-9 for phases to be considered equal. Faults with identical detector and observable signatures are merged using independent XOR probabilities.

The returned spec carries the original horizon: extraction_rounds + 1, including the distinct final readout round. A caller may replace num_rounds to repeat the validated bulk phase over another horizon, subject to the spec’s minimum_rounds(). Characterizing a bounded representative circuit and then retargeting the result avoids building a long dense DEM. This structural comparison is not a proof of repetition for arbitrary circuit families; callers must establish that their circuit repeats.

The input matrices and measurement maps are validated before indexing. Measurement-map rows must be sorted and unique. Shared error_ids are rejected: dem_chunks does not preserve cross-column exclusivity. The raw measurement-to-observable map is validated but is not included in the returned spec, whose O maps faults, not raw measurements.

Throws:

  • std::invalid_argument – for invalid dimensions, mappings, probabilities, locality, missing repetition, unsupported correlated columns, or a phase with no faults. Zero-fault phases require separate support in extended_dem and are not fabricated by adding dummy faults.

  • std::overflow_error – when a dimension exceeds the index format.

std::tuple<cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t>, cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t>> cudaq::qec::dem_sampler::cpu::sample_dem(const cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t> &check_matrix, std::size_t numShots, const std::vector<double> &error_probabilities)

Sample measurements from a check matrix (CPU, per-mechanism probs)

Parameters:

  • check_matrix – Binary matrix [num_checks × num_error_mechanisms]

  • numShots – Number of measurement shots

  • error_probabilities – Per-error-mechanism probabilities

Returns:

(checks [numShots × num_checks], errors [numShots × num_mechanisms])

std::tuple<cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t>, cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t>> cudaq::qec::dem_sampler::cpu::sample_dem(const cudaqx::tensor<uint8_t> &check_matrix, std::size_t numShots, const std::vector<double> &error_probabilities, unsigned seed)

Sample measurements from a check matrix with seed (CPU)

GPU sampling (device pointers, requires cuStabilizer):

bool cudaq::qec::dem_sampler::gpu::sample_dem(const uint8_t *d_check_matrix, size_t num_checks, size_t num_error_mechanisms, const double *d_error_probabilities, size_t num_shots, unsigned seed, uint8_t *d_checks_out, uint8_t *d_errors_out, std::uintptr_t stream_handle = 0)

GPU DEM sampling with caller-provided device pointers.

The function composes (all GPU memory is allocated and freed internally per call):

  1. pack_check_matrix_rowwise (dense uint8 → bitpacked uint32)

  2. custabilizerSampleProbArraySparseCompute (sparse Bernoulli sampling)

  3. custabilizerGF2SparseDenseMatrixMultiply (syndrome = errors * H^T)

  4. unpack_syndromes_gpu (bitpacked uint32 → uint8)

  5. csr_to_dense_fused (CSR errors → dense uint8)

Parameters:

  • d_check_matrix – Device pointer [num_checks × num_error_mechanisms]

  • num_checks – Number of checks (rows of H)

  • num_error_mechanisms – Number of error mechanisms (columns of H)

  • d_error_probabilities – Device pointer [num_error_mechanisms]

  • num_shots – Number of samples

  • seed – RNG seed

  • d_checks_out – Device pointer [num_shots × num_checks] (OUTPUT)

  • d_errors_out – Device pointer [num_shots × num_error_mechanisms] (OUT)

  • stream_handle – Optional CUDA stream handle (uintptr_t cast), 0 for default stream

Returns:

true on success, false if cuStabilizer is unavailable

Legacy convenience wrappers (delegate to cpu::sample_dem; prefer the dem_sampler::cpu::sample_dem overloads above):

  • error_probabilities – Per-error-mechanism Bernoulli probabilities

Returns:

Tuple of (checks, errors)

enum class cudaq::qec::decoder_model_source : std::uint8_t

Authoritative representation from which a decoder model originates.

A chunked DEM is the compact source: a decoder that consumes chunks reads them through dem_chunks(), and the handle carries the closed matrices only when built with from_dem_chunks_closed(). A further source is added the same way, with a new enumerator plus its typed constructor and accessor, changing neither the decoder_init object layout nor the decoder factory signature.

Values:

enumerator matrices
enumerator stim_dem
enumerator dem_chunks
struct decoder_inputs

Finalized decoder inputs: a canonicalized DEM and measurement maps.

class decoder_init

Stable, owning input contract shared by offline and server decoders.

This is a small immutable value handle. Copies share the same model state; the decoder factory takes the handle by value and the decoder base retains it. Source-specific data is authoritative and the common matrix accessors expose its projection, stored when the handle is constructed. A chunked source built by from_dem_chunks() has none (see has_matrices()). Model matrices are stored sparsely instead of composing detector_error_model, whose matrix fields are dense tensors.

O and D are passed through untouched, and the authoritative source is retained. Consumers that need a canonical H should ask for it here rather than rebuilding a matrix-authoritative handle by hand.

static decoder_init from_dem_chunks(dem_chunks_spec spec, std::optional<sparse_binary_matrix> measurement_to_detectors = std::nullopt)

Construct from an authoritative chunked DEM, without its closed model.

For a decoder that consumes dem_chunks(). The dimensions are those of dem_close_all over the spec’s chunks, computed from its phases alone, and nothing proportional to the shot’s error mechanisms is stored. The matrix accessors throw; a decoder that needs them takes from_dem_chunks_closed() instead. Projecting an error frame onto observables does not need them: dem_chunks_to_o_chunked() reads the mapping straight out of dem_chunks().

Parameters:

  • measurement_to_detectors – Optional D, one row per detector.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – If the spec does not validate or expand, or D has the wrong row count.

static decoder_init from_dem_chunks_closed(dem_chunks_spec spec, std::optional<sparse_binary_matrix> measurement_to_detectors = std::nullopt)

Construct from an authoritative chunked DEM together with its closed model.

As from_dem_chunks(), and H, O and the error rates are the model dem_close_all closes the chunks to, built sparsely here. Any decoder accepts this handle; a chunk-native one still reads dem_chunks().

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – As from_dem_chunks().

Declare only a source whose matrices are too costly to build unconditionally &#8212; a chunked DEM, whose closure grows with the round count. virtual std::vector<decoder_result> decode_batch(const std::vector<std::vector<float_t>> &syndrome, std::optional<cudaqx::heterogeneous_map> &batch_opt_results)

Decode multiple independent syndromes, additionally returning results that describe the batch as a whole rather than any single shot.

Per-shot data belongs in decoder_result::opt_results. This overload exists for data that is naturally batch-wide: returning it once as flat batch-indexed arrays is more efficient to produce and to consume than splitting it into one small map entry per shot.

The default implementation forwards to the single-argument overload and leaves batch_opt_results empty, so decoders that have no batch-level data need not override this. Decoders that override either overload should pull both into scope with using decoder::decode_batch; to avoid overload hiding.

Parameters:

  • syndrome – A vector of N syndrome measurements where the floating point value is the probability that the syndrome measurement is a |1>.

  • batch_opt_results – Output parameter receiving batch-level results, or left unset if the decoder produces none.

Returns:

One result per input satisfying the instance’s construction-time output contract.

void initialize_streaming_layout(std::size_t num_syndromes_per_round, std::vector<std::size_t> detector_layer_offsets)

Declare that this decoder consumes its realtime input as a stream of detector layers rather than one full syndrome per decode.

Everything the realtime path can derive from the model &#8212; D, the measurement buffer, the detector buffers, the corrections buffer &#8212; is sized by the base constructor from decoder_init. Layer geometry is the exception: it is a property of how the decoder consumes rounds, not of the model, and the base cannot ask a subclass for it while the subclass is still being constructed. A streaming decoder therefore hands it over here, from its own constructor.

Parameters:

  • num_syndromes_per_round – Width of the widest detector layer, which bounds the per-layer buffers.

  • detector_layer_offsets – Offsets [0, w0, w0+w1, ...]; back() must equal the model’s detector count.

Throws:

A decoding_task_graph is a decoder pipeline of nodes wired by edges. Build one with from_spec (one decoder in a window), combine (two decoders whose corrections are XORed) or from_topology (any nodes and edges). Run it on complete shots with run and run_batch, or stream rounds with enqueue_syndrome. See the Decoding Task Graphs, its Reference section, and the Getting Started with a Decoding Task Graph.

struct task_graph_ensemble_spec

The members and join of a node of kind ensemble (task_graph_node_config::ensemble): member subgraphs run concurrently and one answer is kept. from_topology() lowers the node into an ensemble_fanout, ensemble_join, and the members. Every member node input that accepts a candidate_sink is wired to the ensemble’s candidate sink and every one that accepts a cancellation_token to its cancellation token. A member whose edges reach output (a logical_outcome) has that value pushed into the sink.

The pattern node has one input, input, and one output, output. Whatever feeds input (a shot, or a streaming producer’s windows of measurements or detection events) is passed to every member.

class candidate_sink

push() is thread-safe. It allocates a node, takes a mutex when the candidate may be the cheapest so far, and then runs the observer on the pushing thread.

class selection_strategy

One instance serves one run: the fan-out builds a new one from the registered factory each time it arms a run, so overlapping runs never share a strategy. begin() is called once, when the run is armed, and takes the cancellation source and candidate sink by reference, so that the strategy can request stops and poll candidates. On the pushing member’s thread and possibly concurrently, offer() is called for every push, where a value commits the run to it and hard-stops the other members; a strategy commits at most once per run and ignores every candidate after that. finish() once every member has finished and nothing committed, where a value commits and std::nullopt is a miss.

struct task_graph_output_progress

Progress of one named graph output. generation is a monotonic publication watermark. It advances when every contributor to this output has published its next update. When every contributor reports the rounds it has committed, it advances instead whenever the output’s coverage grows. Consuming corrections preserves this watermark but changes status to pending; generation alone never implies that a value is currently readable.

Public Members

std::vector<std::uint8_t> released

Logical output only: 1 per bit once that logical measurement is final (its readout has arrived and every correction that can flip it is committed). Empty for a correction output.

struct task_graph_streaming_result

Graph-owned streaming result. values contains all named outputs at their declared offsets. Synchronous graphs return a live graph-owned view that must not be read concurrently with graph activity. Async-streaming graphs return a stable reader snapshot after synchronizing the accepted prefix. Copy either form to retain a historical result across later graph calls. operation_completed is an edge-triggered indication that the latest synchronized public enqueue advanced the aggregate barrier; level-triggered readability is determined by status: only available or complete is readable (and either necessarily has a nonzero generation). Consuming corrections changes status to pending but deliberately preserves generation as a monotonic publication watermark for detecting the next update. Generation alone must therefore never be used as a readiness test. result_revision advances whenever any output or graph status changes. completed_operations counts public enqueue operations that advanced the aggregate result, even when several complete before the next read. An asynchronous graph counts them as a synchronous one would. Only reset_decoder() advances shot_epoch.

A logical output, when present, comes last in values; the aggregate generation, status and closure cover the correction outputs only.

struct task_graph_options

Construction-time execution policy for a decoding task graph.

Public Members

bool async_streaming = false

Process streaming records on the graph’s persistent coordinator thread. Records then overlap: a later record runs ahead on nodes that finished the earlier ones, up to 16 records in flight, or the queue’s capacity if smaller.

std::size_t async_queue_capacity = 32

Maximum public enqueue operations queued or executing: how far the producer may run ahead of the graph. Must be nonzero when asynchronous. A windowed graph admits queued rounds together, so a deeper queue lets it catch up in larger batches, but a graph that falls behind returns FINAL’s result only after draining it. 32 keeps that backlog to tens of microseconds while still batching; each slot holds one enqueue.

int async_coordinator_cpu = -1

CPU reserved for the asynchronous coordinator, or -1 to inherit the constructing thread’s affinity. This pins only the coordinator; decoder pool workers retain their separately configured affinity.

std::size_t async_spin_pause_iters = 0

Pause iterations before an active coordinator parks for more input. Zero disables spinning.

std::optional<std::size_t> async_num_workers

Pool threads that run node fires in an asynchronous graph, not counting the coordinator. Unset sizes the pool from the graph: its parallel width, including every fire pool’s copies, or, with an indexed node, every copy that may fire at once (an indexed node’s single copy too) plus the worker its fires leave free, capped by hardware concurrency. Must be at least one when set. Synchronous graphs ignore it.

std::vector<int> async_worker_cpus

CPUs those threads are pinned to, round-robin (Linux only). Empty inherits the process’s affinity. A CPU listed twice or shared with async_coordinator_cpu is an error; one shared with another decoder’s asynchronous graph is a warning. Synchronous graphs ignore it.

class decoding_task_graph

Decode pipeline as a composable, testable object.

Owns one or more decoder plugins and the D/O matrices that connect raw measurement bits to detector events and observables.

Streaming interface:

  • enqueue_syndrome supplies raw measurement chunks to streaming-capable source nodes. Window nodes accumulate them; native-streaming nodes forward each public call to their inner decoder. Published node outputs then flow through the streaming DAG.

One-shot execution:

  • run() walks the internal node/edge DAG for one full shot.

Asynchronous execution:

  • run_async() returns one future for the shot. Independent ready nodes in a multi-node DAG may execute concurrently.

Batch execution:

  • run_batch() walks the graph once for each supplied shot.

The decoders are stateful: do not call into the same graph from two threads, collect one run_async before starting the next, and do not overlap streaming with one-shot calls. Overlap is detected rather than serialised &#8212; an overlapping call throws std::logic_error. An async-streaming graph instead has one internal coordinator that dispatches records to pool workers; its public streaming calls provide copied input and coherent snapshots. Records overlap, a bounded number at once, but each node still sees them in order and every value a record moves between nodes is buffered per record.

Public Functions

decoding_task_graph(std::unique_ptr<decoder> dec, std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>> d_sparse, std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>> o_sparse, task_graph_options options = {})

Construct from an already-built decoder and D/O in nested-row form.

Uses a fixed-T window: the full D matrix is applied once per decode, and the accumulation buffer is exactly d_sparse column-width bytes.

Parameters:

  • dec – Inner decoder plugin.

  • d_sparse – Measurement-to-detector map (CSR row form).

  • o_sparse – Observable-flip map (CSR row form).

  • options – Construction-time execution policy.

bool enqueue_syndrome(const uint8_t *syndrome, std::size_t len)

Accumulate one round of measurement syndromes.

Returns true when any window fired (D → decode → O). For independently progressing outputs this does not mean that an aggregate result is ready; inspect streaming_result() for output and operation status. For fixed-T, a window fires once when its full buffer is filled. For sliding-window, it fires every stride rounds once the buffer is full.

Any chunking works: the graph meters a chunk to each node’s remaining room, so one call may drive several fires. get_num_msyn_per_round() is the chunk to prefer, not a limit. Unlike decoder::enqueue_syndrome, which still ignores a chunk that does not fit, nothing is dropped here.

With construction-time asynchronous streaming enabled, a BULK call returns false after copying its input into the bounded queue; call streaming_result() to wait for accepted input and inspect completion. If the queue is full, this call waits only until one slot is available. A FINAL call waits for all accepted input and the final flush before returning.

Throws:

std::logic_error – if the graph’s streaming routes or effective output schedules are incompatible. Batch execution remains valid.

bool enqueue_syndrome(const uint8_t *syndrome, std::size_t len, round_type type)

Same, carrying the round’s shape. A FINAL round commits whatever a guarded window is still withholding, so the tail of a shot is not lost. Returns true if a window fired or a tail was committed.

FINAL ends the shot: further rounds are warned about and dropped until clear_corrections() or reset_decoder(), because the rounds it committed are the ones the next window’s core would commit and corrections accumulate by XOR.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – if a FINAL round is empty: it carries the shot’s final measurements.

const uint8_t *get_obs_corrections() const

Host-accessible corrections buffer (num_observables bytes).

During synchronous streaming, this is a current-value read between calls to enqueue_syndrome(): an output appears as soon as its node fires, and one whose node has not fired yet reads as zero &#8212; indistinguishable from a genuine zero. For an async-streaming graph it waits for records accepted before the call, then returns a coherent coordinator snapshot without closing the session or flushing it. It never aliases state the coordinator mutates. Its pointer remains valid only until the next result accessor or mutating graph call; copy the bytes if they must outlive either.

Throws:

std::logic_error – If streaming is unsupported or, for a synchronous graph, another graph operation is in flight.

const uint8_t *get_logical_measurements() const

Host-accessible logical measurements buffer (get_num_logical_measurements() bytes): the raw logical readout with the corrections applied, from the graph’s logical output. Null until all are released (by FINAL at the latest) and after the shot is consumed; otherwise as get_obs_corrections().

Throws:

std::logic_error – If the graph has no logical output, streaming is unsupported or, for a synchronous graph, another graph operation is in flight.

const uint8_t *get_logical_measurements(std::size_t first, std::size_t count) const

Logical measurements [first, first + count), or null until all of them are released.

Throws:

std::out_of_range – If the range is empty or runs past get_num_logical_measurements(); otherwise as get_logical_measurements().

const task_graph_streaming_result &streaming_result() const

Return values and per-output publication state from the latest streaming operation. A zero-valued output is distinguishable from an unavailable one through its status and generation. Coverage is the half-open round range incorporated by the latest generation. The returned reference is a live view for synchronous graphs. For async-streaming graphs, each call waits for records accepted before the call, then refreshes a stable reader-owned snapshot; copy it before another result accessor call if a historical snapshot is required.

Throws:

std::logic_error – If streaming is unsupported or, for a synchronous graph, another graph operation is in flight.

void clear_corrections()

Consume the current corrections without starting a new result epoch.

This zeroes values and marks aggregate and output statuses pending, but preserves sliding-window overlap, coverage, and generation watermarks so streaming can continue and the next publication can be detected. Use reset_decoder() instead to start a clean shot epoch. For an asynchronous graph, this first drains all accepted records without flushing guarded tails.

Throws:

  • std::logic_error – If another graph operation is in flight, or the graph has a logical output and its shot has not ended.

  • std::runtime_error – If asynchronous processing failed.

void reset_decoder()

Reset all per-shot state (accumulation buffer, corrections) on every node. For an asynchronous graph, this first cancels queued records and waits for any currently executing decoder call to return.

Throws:

std::logic_error – If another graph operation is in flight.

std::size_t get_num_msyn_per_decode() const

Total syndrome bytes per full window (= buffer capacity). This is what the first decode of a shot consumes; a slid window then fires every stride rounds. Nodes reading the stream may hold windows of different sizes, in which case this is the largest, i.e. the bytes needed before every one of them has fired.

std::size_t get_num_msyn_per_round() const

Common syndrome-byte unit used by the graph’s streaming schedules. This is the preferred chunk size, not an enqueue limit; for variable-width native rounds it may be a common divisor of caller-visible round sizes. A window that does not slide also accepts get_num_msyn_per_decode() per call.

std::size_t get_num_observables() const

Number of observables (= corrections buffer length), excluding the logical output.

std::size_t get_num_logical_measurements() const

Number of logical measurements; 0 without a logical output.

bool supports_streaming() const noexcept

Whether the compiled graph supports incremental streaming execution. A false result does not affect run(), run_all(), or other batch APIs.

std::size_t async_thread_count() const noexcept

Threads an asynchronous graph owns: its coordinator and the pool workers that run fires. Zero for a synchronous graph.

const std::string &streaming_incompatibility_reason() const noexcept

Empty when supports_streaming() is true; otherwise the first deterministic build-time reason streaming execution is unavailable.

const std::vector<std::string> &output_names() const

Which bits are which: one name per output, in the order get_obs_corrections() concatenates them and run_all() returns them. Each is the sink edge’s to_input, or its producer’s name when left at the default. Excludes the logical output. Fixed at build.

logical_outcome run(const measurement_results &m) const

Walk the node/edge DAG for one shot: detect(m) then execute each node.

Does not touch the streaming accumulation buffer, except in a graph whose nodes decode only a stream, such as a windowed one: that graph runs the shot through its stream, from a reset graph, in rounds with FINAL on the last, and leaves it reset. converged is then whether every window reaching the output converged.

Throws:

  • std::logic_error – if such a graph holds a shot in progress, or a completed shot not yet consumed with clear_corrections(): run() would discard it.

  • std::logic_error – if more than one edge reaches output: a multi-output program reduced to its first output is a different program, so it is refused rather than answered. Use run_all(). The logical output is not counted.

std::vector<logical_outcome> run_all(const measurement_results &m) const

run() for any number of outputs: one outcome per correction output, in output_names() order.

std::future<logical_outcome> run_async(const measurement_results &m) const

Run one full shot asynchronously.

The shot is copied before this function returns, so m need not outlive the call. Single-node graphs apply D synchronously and use the decoder’s own async path. Multi-node graphs execute dependency-ready nodes concurrently on a bounded persistent worker pool. Each node owns its decoder instance, so independent instances may decode concurrently. The graph’s single-flight contract prevents concurrent entry into the same node instance.

Parameters:

m – Raw measurement bits for one complete shot.

Throws:

  • std::logic_error – If another graph operation is already in flight or the graph does not have exactly one output.

  • std::runtime_error – If graph nodes request different CUDA devices. Node execution failures are stored in the returned future and rethrown by std::future::get().

Returns:

A future containing the graph’s single logical outcome.

std::vector<logical_outcome> run_batch(const std::vector<measurement_results> &shots) const

Multi-record version: run() for each element in order.

Measurement-to-detector matrix (CSR). Rows = detectors, cols = measurements.

const sparse_binary_matrix &o_matrix() const

Observable-flip matrix (CSR). Rows = observables, cols = fault columns. Throws for combined graphs (no single O matrix).

The CUDA device every GPU-affine node agrees on, or nullopt if none has GPU affinity. A caller must pin to this device before a node’s decoder runs CUDA kernels of its own, same as detail_affinity::pin_decode_device already requires for a plain decoder.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if GPU-affine nodes disagree on device &#8212; one thread can’t pin to two devices for one shot. Pin every GPU-affine node in a graph to the same cuda_device_id.

bool supports_graph_dispatch() const

True if this graph’s one streaming node supports graph dispatch. Always false for a multi-node (combine()) graph.

void *capture_graph(int reserved_sms = 0)

Capture the graph’s single streaming node’s full decode pipeline (D-apply -> decode -> O-apply) into a CUDA graph. Same void* convention as decoder::capture_decode_graph() (avoids <cuda_runtime.h> here); caller casts to cudaq::qec::realtime::graph_resources* and owns it.

Throws:

void release_graph(void *graph_resources)

This graph’s inner decoder, when it has exactly one streaming node that wraps one; nullptr for a multi-node graph or a node kind that wraps no decoder. Exposed for the realtime session to assign the decoder_id DEVICE-mode capture needs (see capture_graph()).
